Leave-one-covariate-out importance of fitted learners

Source: R/csdg_loco.R
csdg_loco.Rd

Computes leave-one-covariate-out (LOCO) importance from a csdg_fit() result (Lei et al., 2018): in each fold, every learner is refitted on the training set without a predictor, or without a group of predictors, and LOCO is the increase in held-out loss over the fit with all predictors. The refits use the splits, the learners with their settings, and the loss of csdg_fit(); they run through mlr3::benchmark() on the stored splits, so that parallelization and encapsulation work as in csdg_fit(), and the seed of csdg_fit() is set before them.

LOCO measures how much worse the learner predicts when it is trained without the predictor: the information about the outcome that the predictor carries beyond the other predictors, for this learner and training size. Unlike permutation feature importance (PFI), it creates no unrealistic inputs; a predictor that other predictors can replace has LOCO near zero even if the fitted model uses it.

The result reports the fold values and, per learner and predictor or group, their mean with the corrected resampled t interval (csdg_learner_pfi_interval()). It has the structure of a csdg_importance() result with one value per fold, so that it serves as evidence directly: claim_relies_mainly(), claim_top_k(), and claim_order() derive claims from it, whose wording begins with "In refits without each predictor (LOCO),", and csdg_check(), csdg_assess(), and csdg_confirm() check and test them with the same criteria as claims about PFI. LOCO is computed once per fold, so the Monte Carlo rule does not apply; for learners with random elements (for example subsampling or internal tuning), the randomness of the refits enters the fold values and thus the corrected interval. The cost is one refit per learner, fold, and predictor or group.

Usage

csdg_loco(fits, predictors = NULL, groups = NULL)

Arguments

fits

A csdg_fit() result.

predictors

Predictors whose LOCO is computed; defaults to all. Claims that rank predictors (claim_relies_mainly(), claim_top_k()) need all of them.

groups

Optional named list of character vectors of predictors that are removed jointly; names must differ from the predictor names.

Value

A CSDGLoco object, which is also a CSDGImportance: a list with fits, learners, loss, measure, quantity ("loco"), predictors, groups, repetitions (1), pfi (per learner, the fold values in the form of csdg_fold_pfi() results), and the tables performance (held-out loss of the fits with all predictors and of the model without predictors), fold_pfi (LOCO per learner, fold, and predictor or group, with type "loco" or "grouped"), summary (means over folds), improvement (per learner), and refit_losses (per learner, fold, and predictor or group: the held-out loss with all predictors, loss_full, and after the refit, loss_reduced). print() shows the mean LOCO with its corrected 95% interval; plot(), summary(), and as.data.table() work as for csdg_importance().

References

Lei, J., G'Sell, M., Rinaldo, A., Tibshirani, R. J., and Wasserman, L. (2018). Distribution-free predictive inference for regression. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 113(523), 1094-1111.

See also

csdg_importance(), claim_order(), csdg_check()

Examples

set.seed(1)
n = 200
x = data.frame(a = rnorm(n), b = rnorm(n), c = rnorm(n))
x$y = 2 * x$a + x$b + rnorm(n)
task = mlr3::as_task_regr(x, target = "y", id = "toy")
fits = csdg_fit(task, list(tree = mlr3::lrn("regr.rpart")), folds = 3, seed = 1)
loco = csdg_loco(fits)
loco
#> <CSDGLoco> LOCO, increase in held-out RMSE after refitting without the predictor; 3 folds
#> decision tree: held-out RMSE 1.55; model without predictors 2.42
#>   improvement 0.874; minimum importance (1% of the improvement) 0.0087
#>   predictor  mean LOCO   corrected 95% interval   folds in top 2
#>   a              0.820           [-0.126, 1.77]              3/3
#>   b              0.234           [-0.593, 1.06]              3/3
#>   c                  0                   [0, 0]              0/3
#> Folds in top 2: folds in which the predictor has one of the 2 largest LOCO
#> values (print(x, k = )).
#> Intervals are reported descriptively. The minimum importance, the default
#> criterion of csdg_check(), is given in RMSE units, because LOCO values are not
#> parts of the improvement.
claim = claim_order(loco, "a", "b")
g0b = csdg_judge("G0b", supported(), note = "Simulated variables, measured without error.")
csdg_assess(csdg_check(claim, loco, judgments = g0b))
#> <CSDG assessment> In refits without each predictor (LOCO), decision tree relies
#> more on a than on b.
#>   Unresolved (exploratory)
#>   Specification (G0a) supported | Measurement and data (G0b) supported |
#>   Content (G2) open | Minimum importance (G2) supported | Procedure (G2)
#>   supported | Stability (G5) supported
#>   Content (G2) is open: on average, a 0.820 versus b 0.234 (difference 0.586
#>   [-0.361, 1.53]); criterion: a positive difference; the lower bound -0.361 of
#>   the corrected interval is below 0.0087. Withhold the claim or supply the
#>   missing evidence, for example new data; where the claim matters, report it as
#>   unresolved.
#>   Decision options: revise or withhold
